funder_name: Fulbright Program, U.S. Department of State (administered with IIE)
funding_summary: The page does not state what the grant covers (stipend, tuition, travel or insurance). It says about 4,000 foreign students receive Fulbright scholarships each year, and that placement and funding negotiation are handled by IIE-Placement or, under Self-Placement, by the candidate.
summary: Programme for graduate students, young professionals and artists from abroad to study and conduct research in the United States. Only non-U.S. citizens from countries listed on the programme page can apply, and eligibility rules vary by country. Applicants apply to the Fulbright Commission or Foundation, or the U.S. Embassy, in their home country. Two placement routes: IIE-Placement (IIE applies to universities for the candidate and manages admission decisions) and Self-Placement (the candidate applies directly to universities and handles materials, test scores, fees and deposits). Degree and non-degree study are both mentioned; the page does not name master's or doctoral levels, age limits, language tests or academic criteria.
route_name: Application through the Fulbright Commission, Foundation or U.S. Embassy in your country
deadline_source_text: No dates on the pages read. The page refers to established country and award deadlines set by each home-country Fulbright office, and to each university deadline for Self-Placement.

programme_title: DAAD scholarship database (study and research in Germany)
funding_summary: Amounts and coverage differ by programme; none are stated on the database page.
teaching_language: English or German (depends on the programme)
summary: Searchable database of scholarships for international students and researchers: DAAD's own funding programmes plus offers from selected other organisations (148 options listed when read). Results are filtered by the country you live in and apply from, by who the programme is for (for example graduates, meaning people who already hold a first academic degree such as a Bachelor's), by purpose, subject and title; a 'DAAD funding programmes only' tick excludes other organisations' offers. If you apply from another country than the one selected, the page says to contact DAAD to check whether you qualify. DAAD does not guarantee that information on other organisations' offers is accurate or complete and advises confirming current terms with the contact named in each programme description. This record points to the database, not to one scholarship: each programme has its own rules and dates.
route_name: Search the DAAD database, then follow the instructions of the programme that fits you
deadline_source_text: No dates on the database page. Each programme lists its own application deadline in its details.

funder_name: Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology (MEXT), Japan
funding_summary: Benefits, amounts and course duration are in the Application Guidelines PDF, which was not read; the page itself does not state them.
summary: Embassy-recommendation route of the Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship for research students. Applicants submit the application form, a certificate of health (completed by a medical doctor) and a recommendation letter to the Japanese embassy or consulate general in their country; the page says not to send documents directly to MEXT. Also provided: a placement preference application form, a field of study and research plan form, and a sample recommendation letter (any form or style of letter is accepted). The application process and schedule differ by nationality, so contact the embassy. Eligibility (nationality, age, education, language) is in the Application Guidelines PDF, which was not read.
route_name: Application through the Japanese embassy or consulate general in your country
deadline_source_text: Recruitment for those arriving in Japan in April 2027 or September/October 2027 is made between April and May of the previous year; first screening is conducted between May and July by the Japanese Embassies or Consulates General. The exact schedule differs according to the country of your nationality.

funder_name: New Zealand Government (administered by Education New Zealand)
funding_summary: The page says 'full academic scholarships' for academic study and short-term training but does not itemise tuition, living costs or travel.
summary: New Zealand Government scholarships to support prosperity and sustainable growth in partner countries and to build lasting connections with New Zealand. Four scholarship types are listed: undergraduate and postgraduate study, thematic short-term training, vocational short-term training, and English language training for officials. The page lists no eligibility rules; it links to pages for eligible countries and eligibility criteria that were not read. Applications are made through an online applicant portal following an eight-step process (check eligible countries and criteria, choose a subject, research courses, apply, learn how scholars are selected, prepare to start).
deadline_source_text: No application dates on the page read; the only date shown is a 2026 copyright notice.
